transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise after 1 week, and that includes gardening. Just avoid heavy work for a month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. I also wanted to ask when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it’s safe to continue using them unless you’ve been told otherwise. If you’re running out, your GP should be able to provide more. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That’s good to know. I'm also finding myself very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: A bit of sensitivity to light can be normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it’s mild, you can wear sunglasses outside. But if the pain is severe, or the eye is red and painful as well, that is not normal and may need checking. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It’s common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after surgery. It should improve quickly and settle down over time. If it’s still blurry, or getting much worse, we may need to check it. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you so much!
